tibetan:
༄༅། །དང་པོ། ༄།ལྷན་གཅིག་སྐྱེས་སྦྱོར་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་བཞུགས་སོ།
སྐྱེས་སྦྱོར་གདམས་ངག་བྲི་བར་བྱ། །
དེ་ཡང་སྐྱེས་སྦྱོར་གདམས་ངག་ལ། །
སེམས་དང་རྣམ་རྟོག་ཆོས་སྐུ་གསུམ། །
དང་པོ་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པ་དེ། །
གདམས་པས་སེམས་སུ་སྦྱོར་བའི་ཕྱིར། །
ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་སྦྱོར་ཞེས་སུ་བཤད། །
problem: The whole title is absent from the glossary. Line1 has ལྷན་གཅིག་; later instances have ལྷན་ཅིག་, and lines20–21 abbreviate the expression as སྐྱེས་སྦྱོར་. Lines42–45 explicitly relate three items and explain the name.
treatment: Use coemergent joining provisionally, coemergent for ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་, and retain ordinary mind, differentiating conceptualization, and Dharma embodiment as distinct labels. In line44 them resumes these three; in ordinary mind renders སེམས་སུ་. The ordinal First in line1 is retained.
uncertainty: The naming relation is locally supported; the exact philosophical force of joining remains open. The glossary has co-emergent ignorance but no standalone joining entry; the compound spelling is not a general approval.
review_action: Review the title and coemergent-joining family proposals; check the precise syntactic force of སེམས་སུ་སྦྱོར་ against a reliable witness.

problem: Standalone བླ་མ་ is absent; the existing Guru Yoga whole-expression entry does not establish a universal English mapping.
treatment: Use teacher provisionally in this work; preserve master-disciple relations through explicit syntax and lineage references.
uncertainty: Scoped working mapping only, not owner-approved terminology.
review_action: Review the teacher proposal; retain existing Guru Yoga wherever that complete expression occurs.

problem: In འགྲོ་བའི་དོན་མཛད་, literal meaning (the standalone glossary output for དོན་) would misconstrue the beneficiary construction. སྤྲུལ་སྐུ་ abbreviates the glossary expression སྤྲུལ་པའི་སྐུ་. Varahi of Uddiyana is the named addressee.
treatment: Use benefit for this construction only; retain compassionate responsiveness, basic space, intrinsic nature, and emanation embodiment. Varahi is a transliterated name without adding Vajra.
uncertainty: The beneficiary construction is clear; historical identification beyond the supplied name is not established.
review_action: Review the scoped དོན་ usage and name transliterations; do not extend benefit to the six meanings at48–52.

problem: Line7 reads དོངས་སུ་ rather than expected དངོས་སུ་. Accomplishment and dakini are technical gaps; the Sanskrit form of the name ལྭ་བ་པ་ is not independently verified.
treatment: Blessed in person provisionally interprets the defective sequence as དངོས་སུ་; no source change. Lavapa is a conservative Roman spelling. Accomplishment renders དངོས་གྲུབ་ and dakinis renders མཁའ་འགྲོ་ provisionally. The subject of all three preceding lines is Lavapa.
uncertainty: Likely typographic defect; identification with a specific historically attested Lavapa remains unverified.
review_action: Check line7 and the name against a witness; review technical additions.

tibetan:
དེ་ཡི་བྱིན་རླབས་རཀྵི་ཏ། །
དེེ་ཡི་བརྒྱུད་འཛིན་ལྷོ་བྲག་པ། །
དེ་ཡིི་བྱིན་རླབས་གུང་ཐང་པ། །
མི་ལའི་ཐུགས་ཀྱི་སྲས་གྱུར་པ། །
རྗེ་མཚན་ལྡན་བླ་མ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ། །
བརྒྱུད་པའི་བླ་མ་རྣམས་ལ་བདག་ཕྱག་འཚལ། །
problem: The lineage verse is elliptical: “his blessing, Rakshita”; “his blessing, Gungthangpa.” The referents of successive དེ་ are implicit. The standalone ཐུགས་ has no glossary entry, and ཐུགས་ཀྱི་སྲས་ is an honorific lineage expression.
treatment: Bracket recipient of where the draft supplies the relation. Preserve Rakshita, Lhodrakpa, Gungthangpa, and Mila without expanding them into historical identities. Render son of the heart as a scoped whole expression, not an approved standalone ཐུགས་ equivalent. The fully qualified lord/teacher is the disciple described in line14.
uncertainty: Beneficiary reading of blessing is likely but elliptical; historical identifications and the precise lineage succession require verification.
review_action: Check the lineage against a reliable edition; approve or revise the whole-expression heart-son proposal.

problem: Line19 has ལྟ་རྗེའི་, an irregular teacher-attribution phrase; the rough reference reads masters of the view. Line17 says the writer fears forgetting, not that a great person is forgotten.
treatment: Following the lord’s spoken words treats ལྟ་ as an unresolved extraneous syllable; its source presence is preserved here and in Tibetan. Render the writer’s stated purpose and future intention, not a completed composition.
uncertainty: The intended word before རྗེའི་ is unverified; lord is provisional at this locus.
review_action: Check line19 against a witness and confirm whether ལྟ་ carries content that should replace the current treatment.

problem: གདམས་ངག་ and the instruction verb/form གདམས་ are absent from the glossary.
treatment: Use pith instructions, with singular pith instruction for the instrumental naming explanation in line44.
uncertainty: Provisional local mapping only.
review_action: Review the pith-instruction entry and its linked grammatical realization.

problem: མཁས་བཙུན་སྒོམ་སྟོན་ may enumerate the learned, the disciplined, and cultivation teachers, or qualify one group of teachers. The speech opening at22 has no typographic closing quote.
treatment: Read three coordinated groups. Quote the immediate report at23–24; the subsequent doctrinal explanations remain attributable to the reported teaching without invented speech punctuation boundaries.
uncertainty: Alternative single-group reading remains plausible.
review_action: Confirm coordination and quotation extent with a reliable edition.

problem: ཉོན་མོངས་པ་ and its abbreviated forms lack a standalone glossary row.
treatment: Use afflictions consistently and provisionally; do not substitute generic emotions or merge them with differentiating conceptualization.
uncertainty: No owner approval recorded for the new term.
review_action: Review the afflictions proposal.

tibetan:
ཐམས་ཅད་འདུལ་བས་འདུལ་བ་ཡིན། །
འདི་ནི་ཚད་མའི་གདམས་ངག་ཡིན། །
མཐའ་དང་བྲལ་བས་དབུ་མ་ཡིན། །
ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པའི་གདམས་ངག་ཡིན། །
སེམས་སུ་རྫོགས་པས་རྫོགས་ཆེན་ཡིན། །
སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཞི་བས་ཞི་བྱེད་ཡིན། །
ལམ་དུ་སློངས་པས་གསང་སྔགས་ཡིན། །
problem: The parallel passage names Discipline, valid cognition, the Middle Way, perfection, Great Perfection, Pacification, and Secret Mantra. Most labels are absent from the glossary; the perfection line lacks ཤེས་རབ་.
treatment: Preserve each classification and its stated causal explanation. Perfection does not add discerning knowing, which occurs only in the longer glossary expression. Discipline and Pacification retain the wordplay with disciplines and pacifies.
uncertainty: Named-tradition interpretations are contextual; the source itself gives no expanded titles or doctrinal citations.
review_action: Review the local term proposals without importing additional systems or claims.

problem: Line28 ends བསྐྱེད་པའི་ས།, literally a basis/place for arousing; an expected causal ending would give a different construction.
treatment: Translate the supplied noun ས་ as basis and supply it is to connect the clauses. Certain knowing concerns differentiating conceptualization as Dharma embodiment. No causal-ending emendation is made.
uncertainty: The noun construction may itself be a transcription error.
review_action: Check the ending of line28; revise the English construction only with disclosed evidence.

problem: རྟག་ཆད་སྒྲོ་སྐུར་ is a compact paired enumeration; only the superimposition family is established.
treatment: Expand grammatically to eternalism, annihilationism, superimposition, and denigration; preserve the two linked pairs and the freedom-from-extremes relation.
uncertainty: Provisional technical expansions; no claim that this is an exhaustive definition of the Middle Way.
review_action: Review the proposed abbreviated-form terminology.

problem: Standalone འཁོར་བ་ and མྱ་ངན་འདས་པ་ are not glossary entries. Their abbreviation at35 is resolved from the explicit pairing.
treatment: Use samsara and nirvana provisionally; preserve ordinary mind as the location in which their phenomena are complete.
uncertainty: No translation of the source into a claim that samsara and nirvana are surpassed is warranted here.
review_action: Review the samsara and nirvana proposals.

problem: ཡིད་ལ་མི་བྱེད་ is an attention/engagement construction. Rendering it as mere absence of ordinary mind would erase the separate mental-faculty assignment. ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེ་ is the metrical abbreviation of the established Mahamudra headword.
treatment: Not engaging the mental faculty with it retains the mental-faculty component and the negation. Good and bad conceptualizing retains the form རྟོག་ rather than silently replacing it by the separate conceptual-thought entry.
uncertainty: Precise English syntax of non-engagement remains a proposed construction.
review_action: Review this whole construction and retain its limited scope.

problem: The source has སྔགས་ (mantra), not བསྔགས་ (praise). བར་ཆད་ལ་ relates the mantra to obstacles; the rough reference incorrectly praises obstacles.
treatment: Render also mantra against their obstacles. Against is the narrow contextual reading of ལ་, reflecting the obstacle setting, not an added claim about efficacy. Spirits and maras follow the two source categories.
uncertainty: The protective application is inferred from the construction; it remains open whether mantra denotes a verbal formula or this instruction as a whole.
review_action: Confirm the source and intended sense of mantra; review the local proposal.

problem: The six-item summary groups benefits and results together and treats the three kinds of discerning knowing as one topic. The subsequent order discusses students before teachers, unlike line49. Line51 contains a double tsheg in འབྲས་་བུ་.
treatment: Preserve the six-fold count and original list order. Read the repeated tsheg as a typographic duplication in translating result; no Tibetan edit.
uncertainty: The grouping is supported by the six ensuing subject areas, not by adding a seventh or eighth topic.
review_action: Confirm the outline against the full text; retain the archival punctuation.

problem: Line55 has སྤྲང་བྱ་, whereas line56 explicitly begins སྤང་བྱ་ and develops rejection.
treatment: Those to reject uses the contextual working reading སྤང་བྱ་, with the anomalous སྤྲང་ retained in the source. Reject/accept preserves the established rejecting-and-accepting family.
uncertainty: Likely transcription defect, unconfirmed without a witness.
review_action: Check line55 and retain the rejection/acceptance distinction.

tibetan:
རྒྱུ་ཡི་དུས་ན་ཞེན་པ་དང་། །
བདག་པོའི་དུས་ན་ལོག་བཤེསཟིན། །
དམིགས་པའི་དུས་ན་འཁྲུལ་པ་དང་། །
དེ་མ་ཐག་པའི་དུས་སུ་ནི། །
རེ་དོགས་གཉིས་སུ་ལྷུང་བའོ། །
དམིིགས་པའི་རྐྱེན་དུ་འཁྲུལ་པ་སྟེ། །
དེ་མ་ཐག་པའི་རྐྱེན་དུས་སུ། །
རྒྱུ་ཡི་དུས་ན་མ་ཞེན་དང་།
བདག་པོོའི་རྐྱེན་གྱི་དུས་སུ་ནི། །
དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པ་དང་། །
དམིགས་པའིི་རྐྱེན་དུ་མ་འཁྲུལ་དང་། །
དེ་མ་ཐག་པའི་དུས་སུ་ནི། །
རེ་དོགས་གཉིིས་དང་བྲལ་བའོ། །
དེ་ནི་བདག་པོའི་རྐྱེན་དུས་སུ། །
དམིགས་པའི་རྐྱེན་དུས་མ་འཁྲུལ་ཏེ། །
དེ་མ་ཐག་པའི་རྐྱེན་དུས་སུ། །
problem: The text applies four conditions: cause, dominant condition, condition of the object of focus, and immediate condition. Some list items omit རྐྱེན་, supplied explicitly elsewhere in this sequence.
treatment: Keep cause and the established object of focus visible; use dominant condition and immediate condition provisionally. Bracket condition where absent from the local source. Immediate is deliberately not expanded into an unsupported temporal direction in this working draft.
uncertainty: Technical identification of the four-condition framework is plausible but no complete canonical glossary mapping is present.
review_action: Review all four-condition expressions together, including whether immediate should become immediately preceding with explicit approval.

tibetan:
བདག་པོའི་དུས་ན་ལོག་བཤེསཟིན། །
ལོག་པའི་བཤེས་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པ་ཡི། །
དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པ་དང་། །
དགེེ་བའི་བཤེས་ཀྱིས་ཟིན་པ་སྟེ། །
གང་ཟག་དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་དང་།།
དང་པོ་གང་ཟག་བཤེས་གཉེན་ནི། །
དེ་ཚོོ་གང་ཟག་བཤེས་གཉེན་གྱིས། །
problem: དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་གཉེན་ and abbreviated དགེ་བའི་བཤེས་ denote a spiritual friend; ལོག་བཤེས་ names the adverse counterpart. Line58 omits the tsheg between བཤེས་ and ཟིན་.
treatment: Use spiritual friend and misguided spiritual friend provisionally. Personal spiritual friend renders the explicitly human/person form གང་ཟག་བཤེས་གཉེན་. Being held/taken in hand preserves ཟིན་. Read the joined syllables at58 with their ordinary boundary for English only.
uncertainty: No evidence that the variants are independent witnesses or authorize a source correction.
review_action: Review the family as a whole and check the line58 boundary.

tibetan:
སྣང་སྲིད་སྣ་ཚོགས་སྣང་བ་འདི། །
རྨི་ལམ་དག་གི་ནོར་ཟས་བཞིན། །
སྣངབ་ཉིད་ནི་སྟོང་པ་ལ། །
སྟོང་པ་ཡིན་པར་མ་ཤེས་པས། །
ཟས་དང་ནོར་དང་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་དང་། །
བུ་དང་བུ་མོ་ཆུང་མ་དང་། །
འདོད་ཡོན་རྣམས་ལ་ཆགས་པ་ཡིས། །
རྟག་པར་བདེན་པར་བཟུང་བ་དང་། །
དངོས་པོ་བདེན་པར་ཞེན་པ་ཡིན། །
problem: Line65 joins སྣངབ་ without a tsheg. Lines66–71 place the list of attachments before the predicates; བཟུང་ is a finite act of taking/apprehending, not the technical noun apprehended object.
treatment: Read སྣངབ་ as appearance for English only. The English clause begins one takes at67 and completes to be permanent and real at70; the list order is unchanged.
uncertainty: Mechanical boundary restoration is likely; no physical witness is available.
review_action: Check the joined source spelling and the grammatical attachment of the desire-object phrase.

problem: ཕྱི་མའི་ཆོས་ denotes Dharma oriented to what comes after, in contrast to this life’s attachments; the rough English outer phenomena loses that contrast.
treatment: Use Dharma for the next life as a scoped reading of the whole construction, not a standalone definition of ཕྱི་མ་.
uncertainty: The immediate context strongly favors the next-life sense; a wider afterlife doctrinal account is not added.
review_action: Confirm this contextual construction in review.

tibetan:
རྟེན་གྱི་གང་ཟག་འགའ་ཞིག་གིས། །
སློབ་དཔོན་ཐ་སྙད་ཅན་ཞིག་ལ། །
ལོ་དང་ཟླ་བར་བསྟེནབྱས་ནས། །
སྒོམ་གྱི་གདམས་ངག་ཐམས་ཅད་ལ། །
སུན་འབྱིན་གོལ་ས་མང་ཞེས་ཟེར། །
ཐོས་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་འབའ་ཞིག་བརྗོད། །
ཚིག་དང་ཐ་སྙད་སྒྲ་ཚིག་ལ།་།

Retain with faith and devotion provisionally, treating the genitive phrase as an irregular or elliptical manner construction; an intended ཀྱིས་ is a conjecture only.
